title: Bake-off (validators): Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
question: Who stands behind NEAR’s validators? Make me a fresh flower with their backers, not an existing one.
note: A real run on NEAR AI Cloud (T060), kept with the signature each completion got. A hash or link the model copied from a tool result is written as a reference to that result ($from, {{…}}), so it replays on recordedClient.

turns.content: You asked for a fresh flower, so I'll make a new one (there are two existing for the same data, but you wanted fresh). Let me read the snapshot.
I have everything I need. The snapshot is reused (fixture, final block), 8,487 participants, 371 validator pools. Now I'll build a fresh flower with the backers segment on.

interpretation.summary: Each bar is one NEAR staking pool, ordered by how much stake it holds this epoch, and the bar is split into the classes of accounts that delegate to it: other delegators, accounts holding 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups. Together the pools hold about 593M NEAR of delegated stake, held by 371 pools. Power is uneven: the top pool alone has ~5.6% and the top 10 hold ~36%, so a small set of pools dominates block production rights.

power_means.claim: Power here is the stake delegated to a pool this epoch (validator_stake_current_epoch): more stake means more voting weight and more block/chunk production rights.

mappings.why: Each pool's share of stake this epoch, compressed into a log band so small pools stay visible against the largest.
Square root of the pool's stake share, standing straight out, so the largest pools stand tallest.
Kind of account, so pools can be told apart from liquid-staking and other kinds at a glance.
Solid for self-declared or verified identity, dashed for inferred, none for unknown, so a named pool is not read as verified.
The point of the question: split each pool's delegations into its backers, i.e. other delegators, 1M+ NEAR accounts, liquid-staking contracts and lockups.
Largest stake first, clockwise from the top, so the biggest pools lead the ring.

conflicts: Petal draws delegated stake, which is NEAR's consensus power. It does not draw governance voting power (House of Stake/veNEAR), operator skill or block-production performance, which are separate forms of influence.
unknowns: Lockup contract owners were not resolved, so a lockup backer is a contract, not a person.
Liquid-staking contract holders (e.g. Meta Pool, LiNEAR) are not broken down to their underlying token holders.
Delegations under 1,000 NEAR are folded into a group row per pool and class, so individual small backers are not named.
424 idle pools (no seat, no proposal) were not crawled, so their delegators are missing.
A named account id or a pool-details.near name is self-declared, not verified, so identities are not proven.
Addresses are not people; this flower is about staking pools and the accounts behind them.
inferred: Some pools (e.g. figment, ledgerbyfigment, bitwise_1/bitwise_2) appear related by name but Petal marks no common-control fusion, so any shared operator is unproven.

turns.content:
Done — a fresh flower, built from the stored final block.

**Flower**: {{call_fa9b6719bb9f41ba92dda0c4.view_url}}

**What you'll see**: 60 bars, one per NEAR staking pool, ordered by stake this epoch, largest at top. Each bar is split into the backers behind that pool — other delegators, 1M+ NEAR accounts, liquid-staking contracts and lockups. The hatched tail is 311 more pools (13.8%).

**Data**: reused fixture, final block 222,915,356 (2026-11-03), 371 pools, ~593M NEAR. Top pool holds 5.6%, top 10 hold 36% — power is concentrated.

**Mapping**
- *width / height*: stake share this epoch (log band / √) — `fastnear-rpc-validators`
- *colour*: account kind (pool vs liquid staking) — `nearblocks-validators`, `fastnear-rpc-liquid-staking`
- *outline*: solid = self-declared/verified, dashed = inferred — `nearblocks-validators`, `account-id`
- *segments*: the backers breakdown — `fastnear-rpc-staking-pool-views`, `fastnear-rpc-liquid-staking`
- *order*: largest first — `fastnear-rpc-validators`

**Changed from default**: only `segments: backers`.

**What this can't tell you**: lockup owners aren't resolved; liquid-staking token holders aren't broken down; delegations under 1,000 NEAR are folded per class; 424 idle pools weren't crawled; names are self-declared, not verified. Addresses aren't people.

Two older flowers exist for this same data — I made a new one as you asked. Want me to publish this?
